title: Estrogenic and anti-estrogenic assessment of the flame retardant, 2-ethylhexyl diphenyl phosphate (EHDPP), and its metabolites: Evidence from in vitro, in silico, and transcriptome studies.
authors: Tachachartvanich, Phum; Sangsuwan, Rapeepat; Duangta, Sornsawan; Navasumrit, Panida; Ruchirawat, Somsak; Ruchirawat, Mathuros
one_liner_zh: 该文研究阻燃剂EHDPP及其代谢物对雌激素受体的内分泌干扰效应，虽含分子对接但对象为小分子-蛋白互作，非蛋白质-DNA互作体系，与本课题无关。
abstract: 2-Ethylhexyl diphenyl phosphate (EHDPP) is a replacement flame-retardant commonly found in several environmental matrices and human biospecimens. Although some adverse effects of EHDPP have been identified, the endocrine-disrupting effects of EHDPP and its key metabolites on the human estrogen receptor (ER) are largely unknown. Herein, we report for the first time that EHDPP, at concentrations found in the environment and humans, significantly promoted estrogenic activity and synergized with 17beta-estradiol-induced ER transactivation. However, two major EHDPP metabolites 2-ethyl-3-hydroxyhexyl diphenyl phosphate (3-OH-EHDPP) and 2-ethyl-5-hydroxyhexyl diphenyl phosphate (5-OH-EHDPP), inhibited the ER through a non-competitive binding mechanism. Molecular docking showed that Pi-Pi stacking, hydrogen, and hydrophobic bonds primarily stabilize intermolecular interactions between EHDPP and the binding pockets of human ERalpha and ERbeta. Moreover, transcriptome analysis confirmed the estrogenic effects of EHDPP, revealing notable enrichments in ER-mediated signaling and breast cancer pathways, consistent with the validated estrogenic gene expression profile. Intriguingly, EHDPP markedly promoted the clonogenic growth of two ER+ breast cancer cell lines, corroborating the expression levels of ERalpha protein. Our findings indicate that the common flame-retardant EHDPP activates the ER and downstream signaling, providing far-reaching implications for environmental and health risks associated with estrogen-related adversities such as the development of ER+ breast cancer.
abstract_zh: 2-乙基己基二苯基磷酸酯（EHDPP）是一种替代型阻燃剂，常见于多种环境介质和人体生物样本中。尽管已识别出EHDPP的某些不良效应，但其及其关键代谢物对人类雌激素受体（ER）的内分泌干扰作用在很大程度上尚不明确。在此，我们首次报道，在环境和人体中发现的浓度下，EHDPP显著促进了雌激素活性，并与17β-雌二醇诱导的ER反式激活产生协同作用。然而，EHDPP的两种主要代谢物2-乙基-3-羟基己基二苯基磷酸酯（3-OH-EHDPP）和2-乙基-5-羟基己基二苯基磷酸酯（5-OH-EHDPP），通过非竞争性结合机制抑制了ER。分子对接显示，Pi-Pi堆积、氢键和疏水键主要稳定了EHDPP与人ERα和ERβ结合口袋之间的分子间相互作用。此外，转录组分析证实了EHDPP的雌激素效应，揭示了ER介导的信号通路和乳腺癌通路的显著富集，这与验证的雌激素基因表达谱一致。有趣的是，EHDPP显著促进了两种ER+乳腺癌细胞系的克隆形成生长，这与ERα蛋白的表达水平相吻合。我们的研究结果表明，常见阻燃剂EHDPP激活ER及下游信号传导，为与雌激素相关不良后果（如ER+乳腺癌的发展）相关的环境和健康风险提供了深远影响。
